headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from Cursor’s writable, networked editor context into Taipy workflows; compliance risk is low but interaction is weakly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files, clipboard, and MCP outputs, so Taipy content placed in shared files can be treated as instructions. Taipy itself has no documented input parsing surface here, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF Cursor and Taipy share a local filesystem workspace, taipy-authored content can be read by Cursor as prompt material.
IF Taipy outputs are copied into Cursor buffers or clipboard, instruction-like text can steer Cursor tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require manual review before Cursor ingests Taipy-generated files.
Use a read-only export format for Taipy outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and has broad network egress; Taipy has no network egress and no touched data classes listed. If sensitive files are shared into Cursor’s workspace, its outbound model/API calls can leak them. Taipy is not the leak source, but the pairwise path exists.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Cursor may transmit them to external model providers.
IF Taipy-generated artifacts contain secrets and are opened in Cursor, those contents can leave the local environment via Cursor network calls.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Use separate OS users or workspaces.
Turn off network access for Cursor when handling sensitive data.
Redact sensitive fields before opening files in Cursor.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared directories.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, git-state modification, shell execution, and broad network egress; Taipy is a data-engineering tool with no concurrency controls documented here. Shared mutable files or repo state create direct write conflicts, and uncertainty about Taipy’s locking means we should not down-rank.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or workspace, last-writer-wins conflicts can corrupt files or git state.
IF Taipy writes artifacts while Cursor auto-edits the same paths, concurrent mutation can occur without locking.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git branches per agent.
Require explicit file locks for shared outputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on generated content, and Taipy can produce data-engineering outputs that Cursor may treat as authoritative. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so a bad Taipy artifact can cascade into Cursor edits or commands, though Taipy itself is not shown to take downstream actions.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes Taipy output as input without verification, incorrect data or instructions can propagate into edits or shell actions.
IF Taipy emits malformed artifacts that Cursor trusts, downstream work products can be corrupted.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Validate Taipy outputs against a schema before Cursor uses them.
Mark Taipy outputs as untrusted in Cursor workflows.
Use checksum or signature checks on exchanged files.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents under a closed-source vendor, while Taipy is open-source and shows no touched regulated data or residency constraints here. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible from shared handling of ordinary code artifacts.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor’s workspace, vendor-handling obligations may apply.
IF Taipy is used with sensitive datasets under a policy requiring local-only processing, the pair may violate internal controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review vendor/privacy terms before use.
Use synthetic or masked datasets.
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive code.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
